ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $ \triangle ABC$, D and F are the trisection points on side $AB$, and E and G are the trisection points on side $AC$. If $DE=2$, then how much is $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $D,F$ are the trisection points on side $AB$, and $E,G$ are the trisection points on side $AC$,\\
it follows that $DE\parallel FG\parallel BC$,\\
which means $\triangle ADE\sim \triangle ABC$,\\
thus, $\frac{AD}{AB}=\frac{DE}{BC}$,\\
leading to $\frac{1}{3}=\frac{DE}{BC}$,\\
since $DE=2$,\\
it follows that $BC=\boxed{6}$.
